terra.problem: Saying the consequence stays with the same person goes beyond the passage. It does not say a person's sin cannot affect others.
The text says clothing, not a coat. Saying bread and a coat are the whole job also leaves out the other actions in the description of the righteous man.
The passage does not say the recipients have nothing or explain the man's giving as not being a way to get ahead.
The text says the recipients are hungry and naked, not that they are cold or that they are not business contacts.
The sour grapes proverb concerns children experiencing the effects of their fathers' actions; it does not suggest that children copy their fathers' sins.
The passage does not say whether the son is making up for anything or give that as his reason for not making offerings.
Comparing the man's turn to serious sin with a burnt batch makes light of the sin itself.
